script.base: No spread or total is saved, so the script is inferred from form and the injury report. PHI is without Saquon Barkley (21 car/99 yd in weeks 2-4), DeVonta Smith (21 tgt/182 yd/244 air), Marquise Brown and center Drew Kendall. JAX's Bhayshul Tuten handled 45 carries for 211 yards over those three weeks into a PHI run defense allowing 4.16 YPC and 9 runs of 10+. Base case: JAX leads by halftime, closes with Tuten, and PHI's committee (Tank Bigsby 27 car, Jalen Hurts 14, Will Shipley 13 in the same window) falls behind and throws to Smith/Brown replacements rather than feeding Shipley.
script.flip1: Hurts keeps it competitive with scrambles (last four rush yards 48, 16, 25, 18, and the L3 trio 16+25+18 equals his 59-yard weeks 2-4 total) so JAX never gets clock-kill carries. Tuten sticks near his 65-66 floor and PHI's replacement backs stay on the field.
script.flip2: Slog or pass flip: JAX's 3.41 YPC run defense and 26% blitz (PHI EPA/db -0.21 when blitzed vs -0.02 when not) stall the shorthanded PHI offense, and if PHI somehow leads, JAX abandons the run — Tuten's carries die and air yards go to Parker Washington (265 air in three weeks) and Brenton Strange.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Shipley under lost because Barkley's absence was the public news and the staff named Shipley the lead back; he got 16 carries, the game stayed close on Hurts scrambles (his week-1 rush spike was 48), and 33.5 was the market correctly pricing a role we could not verify without a when-starter-sat split or a beat-writer depth chart — laying -118 on a 50.5% fair prop was juice, not an edge. Tuten over lost because PHI's missing safety (Epps) and 20% blitz rate let Lawrence throw (JAX EPA/db +0.45 when not blitzed), Rodriguez took the change-of-pace and the closing series (he just had 35), and Tuten finished 64-66 the way he did in the 65 and 66 games. The counter-case is strong enough on price and role uncertainty that neither leg should be sized; the Shipley read is the one that still survives as a flagged strong lean for the human, not an auto-bet.
slip_story: One story only: JAX leads and runs the clock, PHI trails and abandons the run. Stack is Tuten rush over with Shipley rush under. Do not mix in PHI rush overs, a JAX pass-volume stack that needs JAX to trail, or a total under with same-game pass overs. No TD legs. Wicks recyds over is the same trail script but is the wrong market (Kendall out and JAX 26% blitz kill deep yards) and has no price, so it stays off the slip. Main slip would be these two only if the human accepts the flag.
